scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported map covers 1600 to 1878 in northern South Australia. Antakarinja is treated as a spelling of Antikirinya, not as a sovereign state or an exact legal-claim polygon.
The broad Mobile Language Team variant list includes potentially conflated names. Andegerebenha and Antekerrepenhe are not silently merged into this identity.
AMYAC and YNTAC are explicitly separate corporations arising from adjoining claims. Neither is treated as representing all people using Yankunytjatjara or Antikirinya identities.

The community Healthy Country Plan was downloaded and relevant public planning pages read. Only general environmental, food and historical information is summarized; no restricted cultural knowledge, site coordinates or ritual detail is reproduced.
The 2012 scholarly review was read in full. The book itself was not consulted, and the card does not claim direct access to its photographs, oral transcripts or botanical descriptions.
Museum information comes from an indexed catalogue description. The original Gross manuscript was not examined, and no vocabulary, exact collection date or speaker identity is invented.
The Mobile Language Team archive lists restricted recordings. No such recording was accessed or reproduced. The 1967 phase reports only public catalogue metadata.

The 2011 determination is described through South Australian Native Title Services. Conflicting area figures across sources are omitted. Non-exclusive rights are not presented as a grant of unlimited freehold ownership.
The company page supports its 2015 commencement and described processes. Undated staffing, revenue and contract-continuation claims are omitted.
The 2023 strategy and 2022 to 2032 plan identify intended changes, not proof that all targets have been met.
Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
